title: BeliefConfig
description: The reviewed configuration of the opponent belief filter (ADR-025 sections 3 and 5): reviewed data, never code. It names the abilities that can hide a Pokemon's identity and the bounds of the filter's two fail-closed searches. Integers only. Its RFC 8785 SHA-256 is belief_config_hash, a part of the belief identity. A later evidence switch is a minor change within v1; a change of any value is a new record, never an edit.

identity_hiding_abilities.description: The abilities that let a Pokemon hide its identity (today illusion), sorted and unique; each is checked against the vocabulary and a species can hide when its vocabulary ability list holds one. No species name is written in code.

items.description: An ability id of the team vocabulary.

max_legality_redraws.description: The most times a world with an illegal set is redrawn from the next counter block before the sampler refuses (legality_redraws_exhausted).

max_disguise_assignments.description: The most disguise assignments the belief enumerates before it refuses (disguise_assignments_exceeded).

damage_evidence.description: Optional (a minor change within v1; absent keeps every byte and hash of the config, and the belief then reads no damage). The reviewed rules of the damage evidence of slice 4 (ADR-025 section 7, finding N9): how many candidate sets are checked per event, how the engine's display rounds hit points to the shown percentage, which modifiers make a hit non-isolated (and so no evidence) and which candidate items and abilities the probe does not model. Every id is checked against the team vocabulary by the reader; no damage or modifier rule is written in code.

max_checked.description: The most candidate sets (ability, item and named spread) checked per forme and event, most likely first; the rest stay unchecked and constrain nothing.

shown_hp_rounding.description: How the pinned engine's display turns hit points into the shown percentage of an opponent's Pokemon (the forward direction; ADR-018's assumedHp rounding is the inverse, and a bridge test ties the two): a shown percentage above 0 is never 0 while hit points remain.

non_isolating.description: What makes a hit non-isolated (no evidence): a hit of one of these moves, or one of them used earlier in the same turn (Helping Hand); one of these moves used earlier in the channel by anyone, for a lasting effect on stats the reader does not show (Guard Split); one of these abilities held, or possibly held (a roster ability of an unrevealed Pokemon), by a Pokemon in play other than the attacker and the defender (Friend Guard); a move whose target type is one of these (spread reduction).

abilities.description: Ability ids of the team vocabulary, sorted and unique.

lasting_moves.description: Move ids of the team vocabulary, sorted and unique.

moves.description: Move ids of the team vocabulary, sorted and unique.

targets.description: Engine move target types, sorted and unique.

unmodelled.description: Candidate items and abilities whose damage effect depends on state the probe does not declare (turn order, a counter): a candidate that holds one is not checked, it constrains nothing.

abilities.description: Ability ids of the team vocabulary, sorted and unique.

items.description: Item ids of the team vocabulary, sorted and unique.
